name: Braised Pork Shoulder with Fennel and Tomato

fit.note: 622 cal sits inside the 400-650 band (under the 650 ceiling); 7.7g carbs far under 35g; no seafood; whole-muscle braise scales cleanly to 14 (braise a butt). FIT. Source cal is high only because it counts visible fat eaten; a trimmed row would drift lower, safely inward.

dupe_evidence: Not a duplicate. No Italian-style whole-muscle pork-shoulder braise with fennel + tomato exists in the pork catalog. Closest is braised-pork-ragu-over-pappardelle, but that is a shredded tomato RAGU served over pasta (starch dish), not a low-carb roast with fennel. Thai-coconut-curry-pork-shoulder (accepted) is a different flavor family; creamy-garlic-herb-wine-pork-chops (accepted) is a different cut and sauce.
nearest_neighbor: braised-pork-ragu-over-pappardelle (catalog): shares protein (braised pork shoulder) + tomato, but differs on format (whole-muscle plate vs shredded ragu), starch (none vs pappardelle), and finish (fennel-forward vs pasta sauce) = only 2 of 4 axes. Distinct dinner.
cross_protein_collision: A fennel + tomato braise is a portable Italian template. Watch other selectors for a braised beef short-rib or chicken-thigh (Tuscan) version with fennel + tomato that would be the same dish in a different protein.
